How members, months and payments work

Automatic monthly payment = that month’s payout ÷ total members, rounded to paise. For example, ₹100 − ₹4 commission = ₹96; with 20 members the payment is ₹4.80. If the next payment is ₹5, the two-month total is ₹9.80. Total paid adds every monthly payment across the chosen term.

Changing face value immediately scales current bids and manual payment amounts proportionally. Changing members recalculates automatic payments; manually entered payments stay fixed. Blank payment fields use the automatic amount shown in the placeholder. Clear a manual value to return to automatic calculation.

Changing total months updates the table, payout-month options and interest periods. Bid estimates are interpolated across the new term, with a zero final bid; review them after changing the term. Existing manual payments are retained for matching month numbers, and added months use automatic payments. Removed months are excluded from the total. Members and months are independent inputs; unequal counts are a custom scenario and do not verify the scheme’s payout allocation.

Before the final month, payout = face value − bid, with commission included in the bid. In the final month, payout = face value − bid − commission. Commission is a percentage of face value. Use manual payment overrides if your scheme calculates installments differently.

Difference = amount received − total paid. Positive means you received more than you paid; negative means you paid more than you received. Monthly difference = difference ÷ total months. Example: ₹68,250 − ₹80,875 = −₹12,625; divided by 20 months = −₹631.25. A +₹5,05,000 difference over 20 months gives +₹25,250 per month; a −₹5,05,000 difference gives −₹25,250 per month. This is an average gain or shortfall, separate from the monthly installment.

Monthly rate = (amount received − total paid) ÷ amount received × 100 ÷ total months. Annual rate = monthly rate × 12. Both keep the positive or negative sign. For ₹68,250 received and ₹80,875 paid over 20 months, the monthly rate is −0.92% and the simple annual rate is −11.10%. These are simple annualized comparisons, not compounded rates or cash-flow IRR.

How these estimates work

EMI uses a fixed annual rate, monthly reducing-balance interest and month-end payments. Extra payments start in month one and shorten the term. Fees, taxes and penalties are excluded unless explicitly entered. Flat interest uses the original principal throughout. Loan comparison measures total cash paid, not APR or present value.

Chit figures cover one auction. Organizer commission is included in the auction discount; the remaining discount is shared equally among all members, including the winner. Members equal installments. Actual scheme rules can differ, and future discounts are unknown.
